releaseNotes: Made the operating loop graph-native. The frontier deliberately treats succeeded as terminal — correct for launch work, fatal for operation: the weekly rhythm the post-launch doctrine demands (and check:post-launch enforces on wall-clock time) had no mechanism to re-offer the work once a node first succeeded. Catalog workflows can now declare recurrenceDays, and reopenRecurringNodes reopens a succeeded recurring node to stale once its cadence elapses since the last completed attempt — prior acceptance and output bindings deliberately stay (last cycle's work remains real, and the execution boundary keeps exporting it) until the re-run's own acceptance replaces them. A lane-seeded success with no attempts counts its cadence from the run's creation, so an imported mid-launch business starts its rhythm at adoption. The Weekly Ops Review and the Fastlane weekly iteration loop both carry recurrenceDays: 7, and the read-only planner applies the same reopening so its report matches a real session.

Routed the schedule installer into the graph. core/adapters/install-schedule.ts (real crontab/launchd installation, dry-run-first) existed with no catalog node ever telling an agent it exists — the audit's named bug class, built capability the entrypoint never routes to. The new workflow.operations.scheduled-autonomy-installation node (phase 6b, lane post_launch_ops, founder-approval-gated because a standing schedule on the founder's machine is their call every time) walks the dry-run in front of the founder, applies only after approval, verifies with the command the dry run prints, and records mechanism, cadence, runtime, verify and uninstall commands in operations/SCHEDULE.md — with the note that the control-file kill switch stops every scheduled session cold even while the OS keeps firing. Bound into the post-launch-operations knowledge package, whose new Standing Session section documents both halves of the loop.

Fixture coverage: recurrence reopening (due reopens with acceptance intact and returns to the frontier; not-due and non-recurring nodes never reopen; lane-seeded success counts from run creation) joins the verification-sweep suite.
